comp_0.description:
What it does The exit of the Conditional Router template. It returns whatever the chosen branch produced.

How it works Takes the data reaching it from the branch that ran and returns it as the result of the nested run, so the parent flow continues with it. It adds nothing of its own.

Configure Nothing.

In and out In: the output of the branch that ran. Out: the same data, as the template's result.

Use it when It comes with the Conditional Router template. You do not add it separately.

comp_1.description:
What it does The engine of the Conditional Router template. It holds the branches and selects the one to run.

How it works Each branch slot holds one component and carries a condition. The FSM asks its policy to evaluate the conditions against the current data, then runs only the branch that was chosen. If nothing matches, the default branch runs.

Configure
- Branches - the branch slots, each with the field, operator and value that select it.
- Default branch - the branch taken when no condition matches. Point this at something that
handles the unexpected; it is the fail-safe path.

In and out In: the data the decision is made on. Out: the output of the branch that ran.

Use it when It comes with the Conditional Router template - configure it there rather than adding it on its own.
comp_1.manifest_yaml:
extension_type: fsm
name: Conditional Router
description: >
  Control-flow FSM. Delegates the routing decision to its policy, then invokes
  exactly one branch slot and republishes that branch's response_data.

input_ports:
  - port_name: input
    port_type: in
    # The generic start forwards whatever artifact the caller supplied, which may
    # be nothing, so its output port declares `optional(json)` and this input has
    # to accept the same. The script holds the inbound artifact in a guarded local
    # so the declaration is true (VAL-CONTRACT-OPTIONAL-001). Mainflow continuity
    # IS contract-validated: it is synthesized from `mainflow_target_node_ref`
    # rather than stored in `spec.edges`, but the gate sees it either way.
    artifact_type_input: optional(json)
    artifact_type_output: json
    response_data:
      routed_to: string - The branch port name the policy selected.
      match_reason: string - Human-readable reason that branch matched.
      branch_response: object (optional) - response_data returned by the invoked branch.

state_ports:
  - port_name: branch_1
    artifact_type_input: json
    artifact_type_output: json
  - port_name: branch_2
    artifact_type_input: json
    artifact_type_output: json

policy_ports:
  - port_name: policy
    artifact_type_input: none
    artifact_type_output: none
    response_data:
      next_state: string - The branch port name to route to.
      match_reason: string - Human-readable reason the branch matched.

input_parameters:
  - name: branches
    type: text_long
    label: Branch Conditions
    default: "[]"
    description: >
      JSON array of routing rules. Each entry is
      {"port_name", "field", "operator", "value"} and the first match wins.
  - name: default_branch
    type: text
    label: Default Branch
    default: branch_1
    description: Branch port to use when no condition matches.
comp_1.name: CONDITIONAL ROUTER - FSM (SYSTEM, READ-ONLY)
comp_1.script:
import perceivo
import json as _json


@perceivo.fsm
async def conditional_router_prebuilt(input: perceivo.primitives.FsmInput) -> perceivo.primitives.FsmOutput:
    # Read branch configuration from input parameters
    branches_raw = perceivo.params.get("branches", "[]")
    if isinstance(branches_raw, str):
        branches = _json.loads(branches_raw)
    else:
        branches = branches_raw if isinstance(branches_raw, list) else []

    default_branch = perceivo.params.get("default_branch", "")

    # Get data to evaluate conditions against
    data = input.request_data or {}
    if not data and input.artifact and isinstance(input.artifact.data, dict):
        data = input.artifact.data

    perceivo.log.info(
        f"Routing with {len(branches)} branch conditions",
        default_branch=default_branch,
        data_keys=list(data.keys()) if isinstance(data, dict) else [],
    )

    # Delegate routing decision to policy
    policy_result = await perceivo.flow.invoke(
        port_name="policy",
        request_data={
            "data": data,
            "branches": branches,
            "default_branch": default_branch,
        }
    )

    # Extract policy decision
    policy_response = policy_result.get("response_data", {}) if isinstance(policy_result, dict) else {}
    next_state = policy_response.get("next_state", default_branch)
    match_reason = policy_response.get("match_reason", "policy decision")

    # Fail-closed: if no branch condition matched and no explicit
    # default_branch was configured, refuse to route rather than silently
    # falling through to branch_1. A user can still set default_branch to opt
    # into a fallback route.
    if not next_state:
        raise ValueError(
            "Conditional Router: no branch condition matched and no "
            "default_branch is configured; failing closed. Set an explicit "
            "default_branch to enable a fallback route."
        )

    perceivo.log.info(f"Policy decided: {next_state} ({match_reason})")

    # Invoke the selected branch, forwarding the input artifact
    result = await perceivo.flow.invoke(
        port_name=next_state,
        request_data=data,
        artifact=input.artifact,
    )

    # Extract artifact from branch result.
    # WORKAROUND: _format_invoke_result drops perceivo.primitives.Artifact objects because
    # it isinstance-checks against app.schemas.run_schemas.Artifact (different class).
    # So result["artifact"] is always None for branch invokes. Instead, reconstruct
    # the artifact from response_data which IS propagated correctly.
    result_artifact = None
    if input.artifact:
        result_artifact = input.artifact
    if result and isinstance(result, dict):
        art = result.get("artifact")
        if art is not None and hasattr(art, "data") and hasattr(art, "type"):
            # Got an actual Artifact object (would work once platform bug is fixed)
            result_artifact = perceivo.primitives.Artifact(
                type=art.type if isinstance(art.type, str) else art.type.value,
                data=art.data,
                mime_type=getattr(art, "mime_type", "text/plain"),
            )
        elif result.get("response_data"):
            # Reconstruct artifact from response_data (workaround for platform bug)
            result_artifact = perceivo.primitives.Artifact(
                type=perceivo.primitives.ArtifactType.JSON,
                data=result["response_data"],
                mime_type="application/json",
            )

    return perceivo.primitives.FsmOutput(
        artifact=result_artifact,
        response_data={
            "routed_to": next_state,
            "match_reason": match_reason,
            "branch_response": result.get("response_data") if isinstance(result, dict) else None,
        }
    )

comp_2.description:
What it does The decision rule for the Conditional Router: it reads the data and names the branch to take.

How it works Evaluates each configured condition against the current data in order and returns the first branch that matches, or the default branch when none do. It makes no calls of its own and holds no configuration - the branches and conditions live on the FSM.

Configure Nothing. Set the branches and the default on the FSM instead.

In and out In: the run data and the configured branch conditions. Out: the name of the branch to run.

Use it when It comes with the Conditional Router template. You do not add or configure it separately.
comp_2.manifest_yaml:
extension_type: policy
name: Conditional Router Policy
description: >
  Internal routing policy for the Conditional Router. Evaluates the configured
  branch conditions in order and names the first branch that matches.

input_ports:
  - port_name: input
    port_type: in
    artifact_type_input: none
    artifact_type_output: none
    request_data:
      data: object (optional) - The payload to test the conditions against.
      branches: array (optional) - Ordered field/operator/value rules.
      default_branch: string (optional) - Branch to use when nothing matches.
    response_data:
      next_state: string - The branch port name that won.
      match_reason: string - Why it won, or a note that the default was used.

policy_states:
  - branch_1
  - branch_2
comp_2.name: CONDITIONAL ROUTER - POLICY (SYSTEM, READ-ONLY)
comp_2.short_description: The decision rule for the Conditional Router: it reads the data and names the branch to take.

orchestration.description:
What it does Sends the flow down exactly one of several branches, based on the data. It is the if/else of an orchestration.

How it works Wire a component into each branch slot and describe the conditions that select each one. At run time it tests the data against those conditions in order and runs the first branch that matches; if none match it takes the default branch. Only the chosen branch runs, so the branches you did not take cost nothing.

Configure (on the FSM component inside)
- Branches - the branch slots and the condition that selects each. A condition names a field,
an operator and a value to compare against.
- Default branch - which branch runs when nothing matches. This is the fail-safe, so it is
worth pointing at something that handles the unexpected rather than the happy path.

In and out In: the data the decision is made on. Out: whatever the branch that ran produced.

Use it when
- Different kinds of request need different handling.
- A quality or safety check upstream should decide what happens next.
- You want one flow to serve several cases instead of maintaining several flows.
orchestration.name: CONDITIONAL ROUTER (SYSTEM, READ-ONLY)
